plotSections.title: Assignment of the Remaining Keystones
bullets: Walker decides that although La-rel was once his home, the Reach better represents who he has become. Glimmen supports his decision.
Plymouth entrusts Walker with the Reach keystone.
Dana accepts stewardship of the Pitel keystone, becoming guardian of the central arch of Atlas.
Ord chooses Feldspar after considering both Feldspar and Lith. Plymouth explains that Lith's people have not lost magic; instead they experience it through folklore, cryptids, and legends.
Ciri chooses Lith after hearing descriptions of the remaining available arches. Plymouth explains that Lith preserves magic through stories despite rejecting formal magic.

plotSections.title: The Remaining Keystones
bullets: After all party members make their choices, only the La-rel and Terov keystones remain unclaimed.
Plymouth says the original expedition had more members and that those absent companions should not be forgotten.
Kit Anger and the stewards of the Child of the Tree will safeguard the remaining keystones until new keepers arise.

plotSections.title: The Responsibility of the Keepers
bullets: Plymouth reminds the party that although they originally sought to protect the keystones from a lich, they are now personally responsible for safeguarding them.
He warns that the keystones are powerful artifacts and must never fall into the wrong hands.
Plymouth says he cannot tell the party exactly how to use the keystones, only guide them.
He hints that accepting stewardship of a keystone has changed each of them in a significant way.

chronologicalEvents: Walker decides to become the keeper of the Reach instead of La-rel.
Plymouth gives Walker the Reach keystone.
Ord is offered Feldspar or Lith and chooses Feldspar.
Plymouth explains the true nature of Lith before Ord finalizes his choice.
Ciri is offered La-rel, Terov, or Lith.
Plymouth explains the differences between the remaining arches.
Ciri chooses Lith and receives its keystone.
Plymouth notes that La-rel and Terov remain without keepers.
Plymouth says the absent members of the original expedition will be remembered.
Kit Anger and the stewards will guard the remaining keystones until successors are found.
Plymouth warns that the party now carries the artifacts the lich seeks.
Plymouth explains that becoming keystone keepers has fundamentally changed the party.

Walker.existing: Half elf dragon rider & fighter. Glimmen is his mind linked dragon.
notes: Chooses to protect the Reach instead of La-rel because he feels the Reach is now his true home.
States that although La-rel remains important to him, it no longer defines who he is.
personality: Chooses based on personal growth rather than birthplace.
quotesThemes: Home is who you become, not only where you came from.

notes: Reveals that her father placed her egg on Midgard for safekeeping while attending to other matters.
Supports Walker's choice regardless of which arch he selected.
Recalls being very small during the party's adventures in La-rel.
personality: Believes home is where people choose to make it.
quotesThemes: Home is where we make it.

Dana.existing: Half elf cleric, most knowledgeable of the group.
notes: Accepts stewardship of the Pitel keystone.
Promises to guard the center of the rings of Atlas.
Chooses Feldspar as the arch he will protect.
Learns that Lith's rejection of magic does not mean magic is absent there.
Chooses to protect Lith after hearing about the remaining arches.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer, friend of the party.
notes: Assigns the remaining keystones to the party.
Explains that La-rel and Terov will remain under stewardship until future keepers are found.
Warns that the party must now protect the artifacts the lich seeks.
States he can guide the keepers but cannot dictate how they use the keystones.
Hints that becoming a keeper has fundamentally changed the party.
personality: Views stewardship of the keystones as a great honor and responsibility.
quotesThemes: The party has become the guardians of the very artifacts they sought to protect.
openQuestions: What changes come with becoming a keystone keeper?

notes: Will help safeguard the unclaimed La-rel and Terov keystones until successors are found.
Its people reject formal magic but unknowingly preserve it through folklore, fairy tales, legends, and cryptids.
Visitors who openly use magic may be viewed as witches or deities.
Strange occurrences from other realms become local myths.
Reinforced as the arch focused on magical knowledge, science, alchemy, and experimentation.
Each assigned party member now bears responsibility for protecting a keystone.
The keystones are powerful artifacts that require careful stewardship.
The lich continues to seek the keystones.
openQuestions: What new powers or responsibilities accompany becoming a keeper?

misTranscriptions.notes: Name of one of the arches.
Ord asked whether the Gilbrick keystone was still available.

openQuestions: What changes occur when someone becomes a keystone keeper?
